steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Dust two baking sheets with flour.

Beat brown sugar and butter together in a bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in egg, cinnamon, baking powder, cloves, and nutmeg. Mix in flour, 1 cup at a time, until dough comes together.
Shape dough into cookies by hand or roll out and cut dough with cookie cutters; arrange on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until firm but not hard, about 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Speculaas Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This speculaas cookies recipe is flavored with a spice mix of cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg. They’re a Dutch holiday cookie that tastes like gingerbread.

review.reviewBody: These turned out great, but I replaced all the spices with Speculaas spice from the market in Delft. Next time I will use a full tablespoon of it.

Most of the speculas recipes online seem so long and complicated especially with having to chill the dough for hours, etc. I decided to go with this one because it seemed simple and easy to follow. I made these cookies last night with a few changes. I reduced the sugar by half and added some cardomom powder, ground aniseed, and ginger powder to the spice mix. The dough was very soft, but easy to work with. I used these new Nordic molds to make shapes. The key is to dip the molds in rice flour or flour to keep the dough from sticking to them. Lining the baking tray with parchment paper was fine. I had to bake these in the oven for 15 minutes before they were done. They are really good and was a hit with friends and the hubby. Next time, I'm going to add some orange peel and see how that comes out.
Made with Bobs Red Mill Gluten Free Flour and worked perfectly.

This cookie was delicious! I will definitely make it again. I did not have a mold or windmill cookie cutter so I decided to roll the dough out to 1/6th of an inch. Then I cut out rectangles and then hand cut out windmill shaped dough and placed on top. I pressed designs on the windmill and then baked! ❤️❤️❤️❤️

We were completely failing when we were making German cookies, but then we found this recipe! The cookies turned out amazing! We were able to cut some cute shapes out of the dough, and the cookies were nice and spiced. We didn’t have cloves, so we used allspice. But overall…great recipe, one we will use for years to come!
My husband's new favourite! Warm spicing and a lovely short texture - great with a cup of coffee.

I've been playing around with cookie stamps, but haven't found the recipe that held the design...until now. These came out great !! They smell amazing, taste great, and look beautiful ! Perfect for our church fundraisers.
They were way better that the Windmill cookies I remember from the store! Highly recommend.

This was fun, delicious and simple. Treated myself to some beautiful springerle molds, but my husband was craving speculaas. These not only look beautiful but taste great. We read the Legend of the Christmas Cookie by Dandi Daley Mackall with the kids and this is an awesome tie-in and activity. Like other reviewers, I used speculaas spice (King Arthur’s) in lieu of other spices.

I halved it . It was EXCELLENT. I used 1 T of speculaas spice which I made some time ago from a recipe long lost. I am going to try this again with some veg shortening instead of or partially instead of reg butter just to see how it turns out. I never realized that one could simply flour a pan! Thanks for the recipe. Husband and I both loved it.
